On a dark desk in the center, two large trading monitors stand side by side, both facing the camera, glowing softly, together occupying at least 60 percent of the frame width, centered. LEFT monitor: a healthy order-book ladder — a dense vertical stack of short horizontal price bars, green bid bars on the lower half and red ask bars on the upper half, filling the screen from top to bottom like a full staircase of orders, clearly readable as an order book. RIGHT monitor: the same order-book ladder but almost empty — only two or three faint short bars near the bottom, a large empty black gap in the middle of the screen, and one long thick red bar plunging downward through the gap toward the bottom of the screen, as if the price fell through empty levels. The contrast between the full ladder and the empty ladder is the whole story: one market has buyers, the other does not, so the price collapsed in the thin one. Background: rows of dark empty desks and switched-off monitors, cold blue ambient light, subtle red glow from the right monitor. No people, no text, no numbers, no letters, no logos, no charts with axes, no coins, no abstract glass panels. The two monitors must look like real trading screens showing order-book ladders, not glass slabs or barcodes. Post-processed: center-crop 1920x1280 to 1920x1080 16:9 + CryptoScope brand mark bottom-left via PIL. (v3 REJECTED by user 23 Nov ~14:49 WIB: two abstract glass panels — left looked like a bright barcode, right an empty dark glass slab with red glow at the base; nothing read as an order book, thin book, or BTC/CAD vs BTC/USD gap.
